newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Tuesday, with the plunging A share markets dramatically cutting the requirements for short-term money, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract fell to 11.05 percent from 16.00 percent on Monday.
Combined volume fell to 5.28 million lots from 8.41 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"The falls on the A share markets made many institutions pull out from the repo market today," said a trader. "If this continues, the seven-day rate will fall to four percent."

Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down today due to selling by some big institutions, traders said. The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 fell to 117.08 yuan from 117.87 yuan.
Combined volume of the nine-contract market fell sharply to 1.31 million lots from 4.64 million.
Traders said sentiment was weak on the state debt markets after months of falls and that a short-lived rebound on Monday due to a stock crackdown could not reverse the trend.
Traders believe the spot contracts would move in a narrow range around the current levels in the next few days.
